scope: Proposition 4.5 (The orbit Hom calculation) of the manuscript “Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration” (preprints/Rationality-of-the-Canonical-Unramified-Arthur-Filtration-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 014 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 eaf8e38720714e23), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. statement: For P, P′ ∈ Ee, the Hom complex between the orbit generators has a finite equivariant calculation with Euler terms  C[ker(e : V → V )] ⊗ HomDe (P, P′ ) ⊗ Λ• (Ne[−1]) ⊗ Λ• (Lie(Ue)∗ [−1]) Le . (4.8) Here the coefficient factor has lifted degree zero; the shifts in the normal and Lie factors add one to the degrees in (4.4). The formula is an equality of alternating equivariant characters, and a finite-filtration calculation bounding weights, rather than an assertion that the Hom complex splits as the displayed tensor product. For pure coefficient normalizations, all nonconstant terms have strictly negative absolute Se- weight. The weight-zero cohomology is H• Hom(MP , MP′ )wt=0 = HomDe,Le (P, P′ )[0], (4.9) with ordinary composition. Before the finite invariant calculation, weight pieces are finite-dimensional and their dimensions grow at most polynomially over bounded-length weight intervals. In particular, the character sums in (4.8) are absolutely convergent on every normalized compact Le-coset, uniformly on that coset.
